body.p: There live a man and a woman, they have three sons. Their father went off at sunset, he didn't come back, he disappeared. Then the eldest son went off, he also disappeared, the middle one went off, he disappeared. The youngest one stayed back with his mother. The youngest one went off, he went looking, he saw Epkachan's bloody horns, in the middle of a pine a woman started singing, the pine moved back and forth. "Man, man, further, even further, you'll break my pine". The man went back home. He came to the mother and told: "I saw Epkachan, who had killed my father, his horns are bloody, the pine is moving, there in the middle a woman is singing". He asked his mother: "Mummy, did daddy have hammers and pincers?" "Yes, he had pincers, anvils, bellows, I put [them] in the middle of the logs(?)". "Bring [them]". The mother went for [them]. The son forged a bow, he made an iron arrow, he stood up, he shot at a pine. He shot off half of the pine. Again he forged, he made [it] more powerful, he shot at another pine that was bigger. The pine broke in pieces. He smeared his head with glue, he strewed earth [on [DCh]: Not clear why 3SG at "ÉÅ¡iËkin-nun". it], he said to the mother: "I'll go to kill Epkachan; if I don't come back, he'll kill me". He went off, he came to Epkachan, the woman started singing: "Epkachan, Epkachan, chirukulde, you brought a man (?), he presses with his knees, chirukulde". Epkachan started singing: "Man, man, chirukulde, further, further, chirukulde, the pine in pieces, chirukulde, he'll break you to pieces, chirukulde". The man came closer, he shot, he killed Epkachan, he shot at the pine, he broke it to pieces. The woman was left behind. The woman said: "Let's go to the jumping(?) place". They went off, they reached the jumping(?) place, the woman said: "Well, man, [GVY:] tukÅ¡alá»ká»ËtkiË = tukÅ¡alá»ká»ËttikiË?jump(?)!" The jumping(?) place was as if it was made of spits. "You jump in front, I can't", the man said. The woman jumped(?) off, the man behind. Jumping he caught up the woman (?). The woman said: "Now the running place comes". They came to the running place, the woman said: "Well, man, run". "I can't, you [try]". The woman ran off, the man behind, he caught her up (?). Then the woman said: "Now the peeing place comes". They came there. "Man, pee now". "I can't". The woman peed, then the man, [much] longer. "Now the combing place comes". They came to the combing place. "Now, man, comb yourself". "I can't, you [make it]". The woman started combing the man's hair with a wooden comb, the broke the comb, she took a bony comb, she starting combing, again she broke it, she took an iron one, she started combing, she broke a tooth [of the comb], the comb slid onto her breast, the woman died. The man went back. He burnt Epkachan in the fire, he went to his mother, he told everything. His mother tore off her lungs out of joy, she died.
